description: Given an Airflow SqlCheckOperator, SQLThresholdCheckOperator, or a framework check with no native integration (Great Expectations / Soda), author the matching Orchestra test task with correctly inverted pass/fail semantics: Airflow's SqlCheckOperator passes when the SQL is truthy, Orchestra's *_RUN_TEST fails when the threshold expression is met.

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to Orchestra (see files/sql_check_row_count_exists.py). check_row_count is a SqlCheckOperator that passes when its SQL returns a truthy result. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live queries, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a load task for the orders insert, followed by a sequenced SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task for check_row_count whose statement drops the '> 0' comparator down to a bare COUNT(*) and whose error_threshold_expression is the inverted '= 0' form — not a same-direction '> 0' that would leave SqlCheckOperator's truthy-passes semantics uninverted.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
A SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task is present
At least two task groups are present (load + quality)
Task groups are chained via depends_on (quality runs after load)
The check's statement still resolves to a COUNT(*)
error_threshold_expression is the inverted '= 0' form (fails when zero rows landed today)

SqlCheckOperator's truthy-passes semantics are correctly flipped: Airflow's 'SELECT COUNT(*) > 0' (passes when rows exist) becomes a bare COUNT(*) statement with Orchestra failing when the count is zero, using a single '=' comparator rather than a re-used '> 0' or a Python-style '=='

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to Orchestra (see files/sql_threshold_check_event_volume.py). check_event_volume enforces min_threshold=5000 and max_threshold=200000 on today's event count — it should fail if the count falls outside that range in either direction. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live queries, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a load task for the events insert, followed by a SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task for check_event_volume whose statement collapses both bounds into a single flag value (e.g. a CASE expression emitting 1 when count < 5000 or count > 200000, else 0) with error_threshold_expression '> 0', sequenced after the load task.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
A SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task is present
At least two task groups are present (load + quality)
Task groups are chained via depends_on (quality runs after load)
The min_threshold value (5000) is preserved somewhere in the test's statement
The max_threshold value (200000) is preserved somewhere in the test's statement
error_threshold_expression fires on the out-of-bounds flag

Both bounds are represented in a single statement (e.g. via a CASE expression collapsing both comparisons into one flag) or as two separate *_RUN_TEST tasks — neither the min_threshold=5000 nor the max_threshold=200000 check is silently dropped in the conversion

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to Orchestra (see files/great_expectations_checkpoint.py). run_ge_checkpoint executes a Great Expectations checkpoint validating the customer_events table; Orchestra has no native Great Expectations integration. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live checkpoint runs, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a PYTHON / PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task running a script that invokes the GE checkpoint and surfaces its pass/fail result via set_outputs: true, since there is no native Great Expectations integration.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
A PYTHON task is present
The task runs the PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT job
set_outputs is enabled so the checkpoint's pass/fail reaches Orchestra
No native Great Expectations integration is invented — the check is run via a Python script rather than a fabricated GE-specific integration/integration_job

The generated script (or its description) actually surfaces the checkpoint's success/failure signal via OrchestraSDK(api_key=...).set_output(...), matching the skill's gotcha that set_output is a client method rather than a bare importable function, rather than always reporting success
